title: Russian diesel heads to Morocco as supply crunch grips global markets
gist: Russia partially lifted its diesel export ban on Oct. 10 after a Trump-Putin agreement, and a ~40,000-ton cargo is reportedly bound for Morocco amid a global diesel shortage. Gulf states plus Russia made up almost 45% of seaborne diesel trade before the Iran war.

insights.claim: Russia partially lifted its diesel export ban on Oct. 10 following an agreement between Trump and Putin to supply fuel to global markets.
insights.so_what: Russian barrels returning is a supply-side relief valve for tight diesel cracks; watch further easing.
insights.speaker: Jack Dutton

insights.claim: A tanker carrying about 40,000 metric tons of Russian diesel loaded at Primorsk on Oct. 13 and is reportedly heading to Morocco, per LSEG shipping data cited by Reuters.
insights.so_what: First visible flows to North African buyers show where Russian product is being redirected.
insights.speaker: Jack Dutton

insights.claim: Moscow imposed the diesel export ban on July 8 to protect domestic supply after Ukrainian drone strikes damaged refineries, and repeatedly extended it from its initial July 31 expiry through October.
insights.so_what: Ukrainian strikes on refining are a recurring driver of Russian export policy and diesel price spikes.
insights.speaker: Jack Dutton

insights.claim: Gulf countries and Russia together accounted for almost 45% of global seaborne diesel and gasoil trade before the Iran war, so disruption in either hits global supply.
insights.so_what: Concentration of diesel exports explains why the Iran war and Russian restrictions together produced a shortage.
insights.speaker: Jack Dutton

insights.claim: High fuel prices are weighing on consumers in importing countries like Morocco, pushing governments to seek relief from the diesel shortage.
insights.so_what: Importer fiscal and political pressure raises demand for Russian barrels despite sanctions optics.
insights.speaker: Jack Dutton
